canonicals.question: How do I connect to a NimbusDB database?
canonicals.answer: Create a database in the console, then copy its connection string from the Connect tab. The string contains the host, port and database name; authenticate with an API key or a database role. All client SDKs accept the connection string directly.

canonicals.question: What connection string format does NimbusDB use?
canonicals.answer: Connection strings follow the form nimbus://<host>:7432/<database>?region=<region>. Query parameters set the region, TLS mode and read preference. The console generates a ready-to-use string for each database.

canonicals.question: How many concurrent connections does NimbusDB allow?
canonicals.answer: Each database allows 400 concurrent connections on the standard plan. Long-lived idle connections are closed after 10 minutes. For high fan-out services, use the built-in connection pooler on port 7433.

canonicals.question: Does NimbusDB support connection pooling?
canonicals.answer: Yes. NimbusDB runs a managed pooler on port 7433 that multiplexes thousands of client connections onto a small number of backend sessions. Point your SDK at the pooler port and keep the default pool settings.

canonicals.question: Why does my NimbusDB connection time out?
canonicals.answer: The most common causes are a firewall blocking port 7432, a missing IP allowlist entry, or TLS being disabled on the client. Check the allowlist under Network in the console and make sure your SDK negotiates TLS 1.2 or newer.

canonicals.question: How do I create an API key in NimbusDB?
canonicals.answer: Open the console, go to Settings, then API keys, and choose Create key. Give the key a role and an optional expiry. The secret is shown once, so store it somewhere safe before closing the dialog.

canonicals.question: How do I rotate an API key without downtime?
canonicals.answer: Create a second key with the same role, deploy it to your services, then revoke the old key. Both keys stay valid until revoked, so requests keep working during the rollout.

canonicals.question: What roles can I assign to a NimbusDB API key?
canonicals.answer: Keys can be scoped to read, read-write, or admin. Read keys run queries only, read-write keys also mutate documents, and admin keys manage collections and indexes. Scope keys as narrowly as possible.

canonicals.question: Does NimbusDB support single sign-on?
canonicals.answer: Yes, workspace sign-in supports SAML and OIDC providers including Okta, Entra ID and Google Workspace. Configure SSO under Workspace settings, then Security. Database API keys are separate from workspace SSO.

canonicals.question: How do I revoke a compromised API key?
canonicals.answer: Go to Settings, then API keys, find the key and choose Revoke. Revocation takes effect within seconds across all regions. Afterward, audit recent requests from that key in the activity log.

canonicals.question: How does NimbusDB pricing work?
canonicals.answer: NimbusDB charges for stored data, read and write units, and data transfer. The free tier includes 1 GB of storage and 100k read units per month. The console shows a live estimate for the current period under Billing.

canonicals.question: What is included in the NimbusDB free tier?
canonicals.answer: The free tier includes 1 GB of storage, 100k read units and 50k write units per month, plus one database per workspace. Usage beyond the free tier requires a paid plan; the free tier never converts automatically.

canonicals.question: How do I estimate my monthly NimbusDB cost?
canonicals.answer: Use the calculator on the pricing page or the live estimate under Billing in the console. The estimate combines stored GB, read and write units, and transfer for the current period, extrapolated to month end.

canonicals.question: When is a write unit charged in NimbusDB?
canonicals.answer: A write unit is charged per 1 KB written, rounded up, including index updates. Updating one field of a document rewrites the document, so frequent small updates to large documents cost more than expected.

canonicals.question: Does NimbusDB charge for idle databases?
canonicals.answer: You are charged for stored data while a database exists, even with no traffic. Compute is serverless and scales to zero, so an idle database only incurs the storage line item. Delete unused databases to stop storage charges.

canonicals.question: How does NimbusDB scale under load?
canonicals.answer: NimbusDB is serverless: compute scales with request volume automatically and there is nothing to provision. Sustained load ramps capacity in seconds. Very sudden spikes can be throttled briefly while capacity ramps.

canonicals.question: What are the storage limits of a NimbusDB database?
canonicals.answer: A single database stores up to 4 TB. Documents are limited to 1 MB each, and a collection can hold any number of documents. Contact support for storage above 4 TB.

canonicals.question: What is the maximum document size in NimbusDB?
canonicals.answer: Documents are limited to 1 MB. For larger payloads, store the object in blob storage and keep a reference in the document. Exceeding the limit returns a DOCUMENT_TOO_LARGE error.

canonicals.question: How many collections can a NimbusDB database have?
canonicals.answer: A database can have up to 500 collections. Each collection can have up to 64 indexes. Most schemas need far fewer; reach for a new collection per entity type, not per customer.

canonicals.question: Does NimbusDB throttle requests?
canonicals.answer: Yes, briefly, when a database exceeds its current capacity window - typically during sudden spikes or hot partitions. Throttled requests receive a 429 with a retry hint. Back off with jitter and spread keys evenly.

canonicals.question: How do backups work in NimbusDB?
canonicals.answer: Every database is backed up continuously with point-in-time recovery for the last 7 days on standard plans. Restore to any second within the window from the Backups tab. Restores create a new database.

canonicals.question: How do I restore a NimbusDB database to a point in time?
canonicals.answer: Open the Backups tab, choose Point-in-time restore, pick the target timestamp, and confirm. NimbusDB creates a new database at that state; the original is untouched. Switch your connection string when ready.

canonicals.question: Can I export my NimbusDB data?
canonicals.answer: Yes. The Backups tab offers on-demand exports to JSON or CSV, delivered as a download link. For large databases, use the export API which streams to object storage in your own cloud account.

canonicals.question: How long does NimbusDB retain deleted data?
canonicals.answer: Deleted databases are recoverable for 72 hours from the Backups tab. After that the data and its backups are purged permanently. Document-level deletes are covered by point-in-time recovery within your retention window.

canonicals.question: Does NimbusDB support cross-region backup replication?
canonicals.answer: Standard plans replicate backups across three zones in one region. Cross-region backup replication is available on the business plan and adds a restore target in a second region with an hourly snapshot schedule.

canonicals.question: Which regions is NimbusDB available in?
canonicals.answer: NimbusDB runs in 14 regions across North America, Europe and Asia Pacific. The full list is on the status page and in the region picker when you create a database. New regions are added a few times a year.

canonicals.question: How do I choose a region for my NimbusDB database?
canonicals.answer: Pick the region closest to your application servers, not your end users - database latency is dominated by the app-to-database round trip. If you serve a single country, check the data residency notes for that region.

canonicals.question: Can I move a NimbusDB database to another region?
canonicals.answer: There is no in-place move. Create a new database in the target region, replicate with a live migration job from the Migrations tab, then cut over your connection string. The source stays readable during the migration.

canonicals.question: Does NimbusDB offer multi-region reads?
canonicals.answer: Business-plan databases can add read replicas in other regions. Replicas are eventually consistent with a typical lag under one second and serve read-only traffic from a region-specific connection string.

canonicals.question: What consistency does NimbusDB guarantee within a region?
canonicals.answer: Writes to the primary are strongly consistent: a successful write is visible to all subsequent reads in the same region. Reads from multi-region replicas are eventually consistent.

canonicals.question: Which languages have official NimbusDB SDKs?
canonicals.answer: Official SDKs exist for JavaScript and TypeScript, Python, Go and Java. All are open source and accept the same connection string. Community clients exist for Rust and C# but are not officially supported.

canonicals.question: How do I install the NimbusDB JavaScript SDK?
canonicals.answer: Install it with npm install @nimbusdb/sdk, then create a client with your connection string. The package works in Node 18 or newer and in edge runtimes with the fetch-based transport.

canonicals.question: Does the NimbusDB Python SDK support async?
canonicals.answer: Yes. The Python SDK ships both a synchronous client and an asyncio client with the same API surface. Use nimbusdb.aio for async code; both clients support connection pooling and retries.

canonicals.question: How do retries work in NimbusDB SDKs?
canonicals.answer: All official SDKs retry idempotent requests with exponential backoff and jitter, up to three attempts by default. Throttling and transient network errors are retried; validation errors are not. Retry policy is configurable per client.

canonicals.question: Can I use NimbusDB from serverless functions?
canonicals.answer: Yes, and it is the recommended pattern: the fetch-based transport needs no persistent socket, so cold starts stay fast. Keep one client per function instance and reuse it across invocations.

canonicals.question: How do I migrate from MongoDB to NimbusDB?
canonicals.answer: Use the migration job in the Migrations tab: give it your MongoDB connection string and it copies collections with type mapping, then keeps the target in sync until you cut over. Indexes are recreated automatically.

canonicals.question: How do I migrate from Postgres to NimbusDB?
canonicals.answer: The Postgres migration job maps each table to a collection and rows to documents, including JSON columns. Run it from the Migrations tab, validate the row counts it reports, then run a sync phase before cutover.

canonicals.question: Can I rename a collection in NimbusDB?
canonicals.answer: There is no rename operation. Copy the collection with an aggregation job into a new collection, verify the counts, then delete the old one. Writes must be paused or dual-written during the copy.

canonicals.question: How do I change a field type across a collection?
canonicals.answer: Run a migration script that pages through documents and rewrites each with the converted field. The SDK batch API handles a few thousand documents per second. Test the script on a staging database first.

canonicals.question: Does NimbusDB support zero-downtime schema changes?
canonicals.answer: Yes, with expand-and-contract: add the new field, dual-write, backfill old documents, then stop reading the old field and remove it later. NimbusDB has no schema locks, so each step is online.

canonicals.question: How is data encrypted in NimbusDB?
canonicals.answer: All data is encrypted at rest with AES-256 and in transit with TLS 1.2 or newer. Backups and replicas are encrypted the same way. Business plans can bring their own KMS keys for at-rest encryption.

canonicals.question: Does NimbusDB have SOC 2 compliance?
canonicals.answer: NimbusDB is SOC 2 Type II audited and ISO 27001 certified. Reports are available under NDA from the trust page. HIPAA configurations are available on business plans with a signed BAA.

canonicals.question: How do I restrict NimbusDB access by IP address?
canonicals.answer: Add allowlist entries under Network in the console. Only listed addresses can reach the database endpoint; all other connections are refused before authentication. Changes propagate in about a minute.

canonicals.question: Does NimbusDB support private networking?
canonicals.answer: Business plans support private endpoints via AWS PrivateLink and GCP Private Service Connect, so traffic never crosses the public internet. Setup is under Network, then Private endpoints.

canonicals.question: How do I audit who accessed my NimbusDB data?
canonicals.answer: The activity log records every authenticated request with the key id, operation, source address and timestamp. Workspace events like key creation are logged separately under Workspace, then Audit.

canonicals.question: How do I query documents in NimbusDB?
canonicals.answer: Pass a filter document to the find method: equality matches directly, and operators like $gt, $in and $contains cover ranges and arrays. Results can be sorted, projected and paginated with cursors.

canonicals.question: How do indexes work in NimbusDB?
canonicals.answer: Indexes are created per collection on one or more fields. Queries that match an index prefix use it automatically; the explain method shows the chosen plan. Writes update indexes synchronously, so add only the indexes you read from.

canonicals.question: Does NimbusDB support full-text search?
canonicals.answer: Yes, text indexes support tokenized search with language-aware stemming over string fields. Create a text index on the fields you search, then use the $text operator. Ranking follows BM25.

canonicals.question: How do I paginate large result sets in NimbusDB?
canonicals.answer: Use cursor pagination: each response returns a cursor you pass to the next call. Offset pagination exists but scans skipped rows, so it gets slower and more expensive deep into a collection.

canonicals.question: Can NimbusDB do aggregations like group by?
canonicals.answer: The aggregate method runs pipelines of stages: match, group with accumulators like sum and avg, sort and limit. Pipelines use indexes for their leading match stage, so filter early in the pipeline.

canonicals.question: What are the NimbusDB rate limits?
canonicals.answer: The free tier allows 50 requests per second per database; standard plans start at 2,000 and scale with capacity. Exceeding the limit returns 429 responses with a retry hint header.

canonicals.question: What is the maximum request size in NimbusDB?
canonicals.answer: A single request can be at most 6 MB, and a batch write can carry at most 1,000 documents. Both limits apply before compression. Split larger imports into multiple batch calls.

canonicals.question: How many databases can a NimbusDB workspace have?
canonicals.answer: Free workspaces have one database; paid workspaces have up to 100. Databases are isolated from each other and billed by their own usage.

canonicals.question: What is the query timeout in NimbusDB?
canonicals.answer: Queries time out after 30 seconds. Aggregation pipelines and full scans are the usual offenders; check the plan with explain and add an index instead of raising the timeout on the client.

canonicals.question: Does NimbusDB limit index count per collection?
canonicals.answer: A collection can have up to 64 indexes. Every index slows writes and adds storage, so review unused indexes regularly from the Indexes tab, which shows per-index usage.

canonicals.question: How do I create a database in the NimbusDB console?
canonicals.answer: Choose New database from the console home, pick a region and a name, and confirm. The database is ready in a few seconds. The Connect tab appears with the connection string and SDK snippets.

canonicals.question: How do I invite a teammate to my NimbusDB workspace?
canonicals.answer: Go to Workspace settings, then Members, and send an invite by email with a role: viewer, developer or admin. Invites expire after seven days. Teammates get their own sign-in; API keys stay per workspace.

canonicals.question: Where do I see slow queries in NimbusDB?
canonicals.answer: The Insights tab lists the slowest operations with their plans, counts and average latency over the last day. Click an operation for the full plan and index suggestions.

canonicals.question: How do I rename a NimbusDB database?
canonicals.answer: Open the database, go to Settings, and edit the name. Renaming does not change the host or the connection string, so clients keep working. The old name is released immediately for reuse.

canonicals.question: How do I delete a NimbusDB database?
canonicals.answer: In the database Settings tab, choose Delete database and type the database name to confirm. The database stops serving immediately and stays recoverable for 72 hours from the Backups tab before permanent removal.
